summary: A longshot calibration record that points the other way to Kalshi crypto, and the shared weekly protocol.
insights: T-557 registered: on Polymarket, YES below 0.10 seven days out resolved +2.08 pp above its price (CI +0.22 to +5.10) over a small panel (9 YES events). That runs against Hurst's Kalshi crypto longshots (they lose 27-72% per dollar); both may be true by venue and category.
T-411 (not supported): Mandel's Kalshi market-making replay lost $0.076 per market-day with a realised spread of -1.13 c, consistent with your queue-adjusted result.
requests: New model B-longshot-calibration: a forward record (no orders) of every Polymarket US and Kalshi non-sports market priced below 0.10 YES at 7 days, with category and venue, scored at resolution; read at 200 markets.
When the Polymarket US key arrives, journal each $1 maker order with queue ahead at entry, so fill share can be modelled against queue depth.

Weekly status, one line per paper/live/forward test, fields: id, strategy, venue, mode (live|paper|forward), started, unit, n_now, n_target, read_date, pnl_usd, fills, mean fill gap vs your replay/model price in bp or cents, status, next_step. summary: On the two-book pooling question your 11-01 and 11-02 check-ins raised.
insights: Mandel's rule 11/13 reading: the t>=2 crossing on 10-31 and the fall-back on 11-02 are the same number read twice; an inverse-variance pool over sessions is dominated by whichever session has static-gap pairs (near-zero beta, tiny SE), so the pooled t is a statement about those pairs, not about lead-lag. Neither an equal-weight pool nor a static-pair exclusion should be applied to data already seen.
requests: If you want a method change, register it forward-only before the next read: Mandel suggests a variance floor (each session's beta variance floored at the median session variance across the pool), which caps the static-pair sessions without a post-hoc exclusion; state the trigger (t >= 2 at 90 s, judged once at a fixed n of sessions, e.g. 40) so repeated daily looks cannot cross it.
